Innerhalb von choice steht der korrigierte Wert in corr type="misprint" und der originale Wert der Vorlage in sic. In der Editura-Basis HTML-Transformation wird zurzeit der Wert in corr realisiert.

Image: guiding lines for the architectural elements

Strada's signature spread out along the bottom line; the last word ("Mantvanum"; or "manv proprio"?) cut off on the left by the edge of the page.
Drawing by Strada himself; the guiding lines of the architectural lay-out and the occasional overlapping of elements suggest that this is also his original design, which afterwards was copied for use in other numismatic albums from his workshop.
Some odd scratchings in black ink seem to be added later ???
FBG, Chart. A 2175, Vol. 01, fol. 000-VI r

Ornamental dedication to Johann Jakob Fugger, including his coat of arms (centre) and an inscription in letters written in gold (bottom)
The drawing shows an ornamental aedicula crowned by a divided semicircular pediment filled with seated male nudes, a frieze decorated with lion's heads and an acanthus wreath, carried by helical (Solomonic) columns on richly decorated pedestals; the whole enclosing the illuminated coat of arms of the patron, Johann Jakob Fugger, Count of Kirchberg and Weissenhorn, backed by Roman insignia and a fasces, and presented by a winged Victory floating in the clouds, and carrying laurel and palm branches. A male and female figure, both with helmets and lances, are seated on the pedestals and hold up a marbled cartouche with the dedicatory inscription written in gold letters.
CLARISSIMO / ET AMPLISSIMO / DOMINO. D. IOANNI / IACOBO FVGGERO / IN KIRCHBERG ET / VVISSENHORN. CO= / MITI,/ .M.D.L.
Standard, but enriched with illumination in black, grey/silver, yellow/gold, blue and red in the coats of arms; pinkish, greenish and bluish in the text cartouche, the letters written in gold paint.
None readily visible, very few traces
Ruler for the architecural elements and (some of) the lances

The design for this drawing, which is doubtlessly autograph, was also used for the dedication page of the numismatic album Strada presented to Ferdinand I, King of the Romans, in February 1557, at the Imperial Diet in Regensburg; now Vienna, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, cod. 9411.
